declared_proposition: For finite-dimensional operators T_j, let H_ij=<T_i,T_j>_HS. Then 1^*H1=||sum_j T_j||_HS^2 and ||sum_j T_j||_op^2<=1^*H1. Therefore the signed cross-Gram zero mode bound 1^*H1<=eta sum_j||T_j||_HS^2 is a sufficient operator power-saving certificate. Absolute cross-Gram magnitudes do not determine this zero mode.
mathematical_argument: Expand the Hilbert-Schmidt square of the aggregate and use operator norm at most Hilbert-Schmidt norm. For scalar operators, the aligned phases and all m-th roots of unity have identical component norms and identical absolute cross-Gram matrices, but their signed zero modes are m^2 and 0. Thus phase erasure cannot certify the all-plus arithmetic mode.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The zero-mode inequality is only a sufficient data contract. It does not establish a power saving for actual prime-pair Haar blocks, and a Hilbert-Schmidt diagonal budget may itself be too large unless arithmetic rank and scale growth are controlled.

discarded_route: absolute cross-Gram magnitudes or average Fourier modes as sufficient statistics for the all-plus mode
remaining_gap: No arithmetic theorem bounds the signed all-plus zero mode of actual prime-pair Haar cross-Gram data by a power-saving fraction of diagonal energy.
claim_boundary: No Twin Prime proof or parity-breaking lower bound; one exact zero-mode certificate and an infinite phase-erasure counterfamily only.
